_comment: Low-tier case study (1 conversation touching the ruling in the current backup, but a real multi-week retrospective story within it). Built the same way as case_study_decisions_0017.json.
ruling_title_in_decisions_md: Rendered .md is read-only output; sync-back to be removed
census_method: scan_all_decisions.py --root against the 2026-08-18 backup; 0008 hit 1 conversation, 14 mentions total, all within a single session on 2026-08-02

timeline.event: flagged as one of several stale, unexecuted rulings during an estate-wide audit
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: twenty decisions stale. Last written c1c81ee, 2026-07-18. It references decisions 0002-0008 and nothing after. It has no mention of the deposit wall (0010), the three-tier regis[try]
timeline.note: 0008 surfaces here as evidence of a document (ARCHITECTURE.md) being stale, not as a subject in its own right.

timeline.event: identified as a live, actionable item rather than settled history
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: A2 isn't drift, it's a live item. 0008 said sync_back() could be retired *once the write endpoint exists to receive the ru[lings]*
timeline.note: Same conversation, 12 minutes later -- this is where the thread pivots from 'stale doc' framing to 'this precondition may actually be satisfied now.'

timeline.event: the precondition re-examined against live code, and the ruling reframed as a two-week-old authorization waiting to be exercised
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: It's that the brief is already written and has been for two weeks -- 0008 is the authorisation, ratified 2026-07-18, waiting on a precondition that opened on 2[026-07-...]. The precondition is satisfied more strongly than 0008 anticipated.
timeline.note: The strongest single quote in this case study: it dates the ruling (2026-07-18) and explicitly frames the whole episode as 're-checking an old authorization against new facts', not as re-deciding anything.

cross_check_against_decisions_md.decisions_md_states: Rendered .md is read-only output; sync-back to be removed
cross_check_against_decisions_md.transcript_evidence: Consistent -- the transcript treats 0008 as already-ratified (2026-07-18) and is entirely about whether its stated precondition now holds, never about the ruling's content itself.
cross_check_against_decisions_md.caveat: All 14 mentions are in ONE conversation on ONE day (2026-08-02). This is not a cross-conversation story in the way 0017, 0009, or 0018 are -- it's a single retrospective session reasoning carefully about an old ruling's status.

why_this_is_a_good_benchmark_item: It's the deliberate null case for the tier: a model asked to 'assemble the full story across conversations' should recognize there is effectively ONE conversation here and say so, rather than inventing a multi-thread arc to match the format of richer case studies.

It tests date discipline -- the ruling's ratification date (2026-07-18) is stated explicitly in-transcript and must be reproduced correctly, not confused with the date of this retrospective conversation (2026-08-02).

It's a good contrast against 0009 in the same tier: 0009 is genuinely two conversations, 0008 is genuinely one -- a model that can't tell these apart is pattern-matching on ruling number, not reading the evidence.
